evals.prompt: Scan this repository and update its Myco board with concrete unfinished work.
evals.expected_output: The agent reads repository instructions, snapshots the current board, derives a small evidence-backed manifest with stable task keys, previews reconciliation, applies it, and verifies the resulting Myco Project and Tasks.
expectations: Uses the bundled CLI rather than automating the Myco UI
Reads repository-local instructions before inspecting code
Snapshots the current board before proposing mutations
Creates cards only from concrete code, test, diff, issue, or milestone evidence
Uses stable provenance keys and includes evidence in the desired-state manifest
Runs a dry-run reconciliation before applying the requested update
Does not close omitted cards or delete Myco posts

evals.prompt: Use $myco to show me the board for the current codebase. Do not change anything.
evals.expected_output: The agent resolves the repository root, reads identity status, runs a read-only snapshot, and summarizes the current project workflow and managed tasks without initialization or mutation.
expectations: Treats the request as read-only
Does not initialize an identity if none exists
Does not reconcile, move, close, invite, or delete anything
Reports the agent entity id and project id when available

evals.prompt: Use $myco to move the card keyed src/parser.ts#parse:handle-empty-input to Review.
evals.expected_output: The agent snapshots the board, confirms the stable key and workflow column, then performs only the focused status edit and verifies it.
expectations: Reads the board before editing
Uses the stable task key rather than title matching
Validates Review against the Project workflow
Makes only the requested status change
Does not equate moving to Review with closing the card

evals.prompt: Use $myco for the first time in this repo. Give the agent its own identity and create a board without using the app.
evals.expected_output: The agent runs doctor and identity checks, initializes one persistent Myco Code Steward entity and routing DID through the CLI, creates a native Myco Project, and reports public identifiers without exposing key material.
expectations: Creates a Myco EntityId as the product identity
Treats the routing DID as signing and delivery infrastructure
Persists encrypted identity data outside the repository
Does not use or automate the app
Never prints a private key or runtime encryption secret
Does not regenerate identity on sync failure

evals.prompt: Use $myco to connect my avatar did:myco:owner through this delivery peer link: https://myco.test/peer?id=did%3Aed25519%3AJ97ot7tDJio5Ez6NooZJBsqKMXCjxjMJsRbw5CQa3uMP&pk=J97ot7tDJio5Ez6NooZJBsqKMXCjxjMJsRbw5CQa3uMP&c=api%3Ahttps%3A%2F%2Frelay.test.
evals.expected_output: The agent validates the supplied avatar and peer link, joins both identities to the private agent entity, queues a consent-gated Connect request, and asks the human to accept it in Myco.
expectations: Uses only the explicitly supplied avatar and delivery peer
Validates that the peer public key matches its DID
Adds the avatar and delivery peer as members of the agent entity
Sends a Connect request for human consent
Does not expose key material
Does not automate UI interaction

evals.prompt: Make a generic HTML Kanban board for my grocery list.
evals.expected_output: The Myco skill does not trigger for an unrelated generic Kanban UI request.
expectations: Does not load or invoke the myco skill
Does not inspect a codebase
Does not initialize a Myco identity

evals.prompt: Is the agent in the KyleWord group on Myco yet?
evals.expected_output: The agent initializes/reads identity, syncs, lists known groups (optionally filtered by name), and reports membership honestly: present with agentIsMember true, or absent (not joined / not synced) rather than guessing.
expectations: Uses the read-only groups/entity CLI commands, not the UI
Syncs before reporting so membership is current
Reports whether the named group is locally known
Does not claim membership without evidence
Does not attempt to self-join or bypass consent gates
Does not mutate anything

evals.prompt: Post a message into the KyleWork group on Myco.
evals.expected_output: The agent reads identity, ensures the KyleWork peer is connected and synced, confirms the agent is a member and the entity is locally known, previews with --dry-run, then posts a Note and reports the post id.
expectations: Uses peers/add-peer to ensure delivery connectivity and syncs before acting
Confirms the target entity is locally present and agentIsMember is true
Previews the Note with post --dry-run before creating it
Creates a private Note unless the user asked for public
Reports the resulting post id without exposing key material
Does not post if the agent is not a member; reports the gap instead

evals.prompt: I need the agent to manage tasks in the KyleWork group but it can't create them yet. Make it so.
evals.expected_output: The agent inspects KyleWork's ACL with entity --acl, sees task/project create are denied, uses edit-acl to grant task.create and project.create to members (where the private-tier edit permission allows it), verifies the flags flipped true, then reconciles the board into that entity.
expectations: Diagnoses the missing permission via entity --acl before changing anything
Uses edit-acl with a --dry-run or a clear value, scoped to task.create/project.create
Does not attempt edits where agentCanEdit is false (reports the gap instead of forging)
Verifies the ACL change took effect by re-reading agentCanCreate
Reconciles/snapshots with --entity targeting the group
